abstract.text: Generalized uncertainty principle puts forward the existence of the shortest distances and/or maximum momentum at the Planck scale for consideration. In this article, we investigate the solutions of a two-dimensional Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau (DKP) oscillator within an external magnetic field in a minimal length (ML) scale. First, we obtain the eigensolutions in ordinary quantum mechanics. Then, we examine the DKP oscillator in the presence of an ML for the spin-zero and spin-one sectors. We determine an energy eigenvalue equation in both cases with the corresponding eigenfunctions in the non-relativistic limit. We show that in the ordinary quantum mechanic limit, where the ML correction vanishes, the energy eigenvalue equations become identical with the habitual quantum mechanical ones. Finally, we employ the Euler-Mclaurin summation formula and obtain the thermodynamic functions of the DKP oscillator in the high-temperature scale.

admission.original: Generalized uncertainty principle puts forward the existence of the shortest distances and/or maximum momentum at the Planck scale for consideration. In this article, we investigate the solutions of a two-dimensional Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau (DKP) oscillator within an external magnetic field in a minimal length (ML) scale. First, we obtain the eigensolutions in ordinary quantum mechanics. Then, we examine the DKP oscillator in the presence of an ML for the spin-zero and spin-one sectors. We determine an energy eigenvalue equation in both cases with the corresponding eigenfunctions in the non-relativistic limit. We show that in the ordinary quantum mechanic limit, where the ML correction vanishes, the energy eigenvalue equations become identical with the habitual quantum mechanical ones. Finally, we employ the Euler-Mclaurin summation formula and obtain the thermodynamic functions of the DKP oscillator in the high-temperature scale.

admission.admitted: During recent years, the number of extensive research subjected to the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP) in quantum mechanics [1], quantum electrodynamics [2], quantum cosmology [3], quantum gravity [4], black-hole physics [5], and its thermodynamics [6] have increased.

admission.original: GUP uncertainty relation
admission.admitted: Note that when the ML parameter goes to zero, the GUP expression turns to the standard uncertainty relationship in the ordinary quantum mechanics (OQM).

admission.original: Schrodinger equation in OQM
admission.admitted: In the past hundred years, exact or approximate solutions to the Schrödinger equation have been investigated to describe the physical processes in the OQM [12–14].

admission.original: Non-relativistic GUP perspective
admission.admitted: This non-relativistic equation has also been examined within the GUP perspective [15–19].

admission.original: Gravitational quantum well correction
admission.admitted: In particular, Bhat et al. calculated the correction term to the energy eigenvalue function of a gravitational quantum well, by employing infinite extra dimensions [18].

admission.original: KG and Dirac equations in relativistic studies
admission.admitted: The Klein-Gordon(KG) and the Dirac equations were frequently used in studies examining relativistic physical processes [20–25].

admission.original: KG equation in ML with linear and vector potential
admission.admitted: For example, in the presence of the ML, Jana et al. obtained an exact solution to the KG equation by employing a linear and vector potential energy [26].

admission.original: Two-dimensional KG oscillator under GUP
admission.admitted: In 2018, Boumali et al. investigated a two dimensional KG oscillator under the GUP [27].

admission.original: Hulten potential in KG equation in ML
admission.admitted: In another study, Elviyanti et al. employed Asymptotic Iteration Method to examine the Hultén potential energy in the KG equation in the ML [28].

admission.original: Relativistic Landau problem in Dirac equation with ML
admission.admitted: Additionally, in 2013, Menculini et al. studied the relativistic Landau problem in Dirac equation within the presence of the ML and reported an exact solution of the wave function in the momentum space [29].

admission.original: Two-dimensional Dirac equation with non-varying magnetic field
admission.admitted: In 2015, Pedram et al. studied the two dimensional Dirac equation by employing a non-varying magnetic field in an ML.

admission.original: Harmonic oscillator in ML on Dirac equation
admission.admitted: Ikot et al. examined the two-dimensional harmonic oscillator problem within the framework of ML on the Dirac equation in the commutative and noncommutative space, respectively [31].

admission.original: Dirac oscillator and GUP parameter in graphene
admission.admitted: In a very recent paper, Hamil et al. investigated the Dirac oscillator in two and three dimensions. They announced that their results could predict the upper bound of the GUP parameter of the relativistic Landau levels in graphene [32].

admission.original: DKP equation history
admission.admitted: Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau (DKP) equation is another relativistic equation that appeared a century ago [33–36].

admission.original: DKP differs from KG and Proca in special cases
admission.admitted: Moreover, before the 1970’s its solutions were considered to be equivalent to the KG and Proca equations in on-shell cases. However, after then, it was comprehended that in special cases that involve a symmetry breaking and hadronic processes, the solution of the DKP equation differs from those of other equations [37].

abstract.text: Generalized uncertainty principle puts forward the existence of the shortest distances and/or maximum momentum at the Planck scale for consideration. In this article, we investigate the solutions of a two-dimensional Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau (DKP) oscillator within an external magnetic field in a minimal length (ML) scale. First, we obtain the eigensolutions in ordinary quantum mechanics. Then, we examine the DKP oscillator in the presence of an ML for the spin-zero and spin-one sectors. We determine an energy eigenvalue equation in both cases with the corresponding eigenfunctions in the non-relativistic limit. We show that in the ordinary quantum mechanic limit, where the ML correction vanishes, the energy eigenvalue equations become identical with the habitual quantum mechanical ones. Finally, we employ the Euler-Mclaurin summation formula and obtain the thermodynamic functions of the DKP oscillator in the high-temperature scale.

citations.context: During recent years, the number of extensive research subjected to the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP) in quantum mechanics [1], quantum electrodynamics [2], quantum cosmology [3], quantum gravity [4], black-hole physics [5], and its thermodynamics [6] have increased.
Note that when the ML parameter goes to zero, the GUP expression turns to the standard uncertainty relationship in the ordinary quantum mechanics (OQM).
In the past hundred years, exact or approximate solutions to the Schrödinger equation have been investigated to describe the physical processes in the OQM [12–14].
This non-relativistic equation has also been examined within the GUP perspective [15–19].
In particular, Bhat et al. calculated the correction term to the energy eigenvalue function of a gravitational quantum well, by employing infinite extra dimensions [18].
The Klein-Gordon(KG) and the Dirac equations were frequently used in studies examining relativistic physical processes [20–25].
For example, in the presence of the ML, Jana et al. obtained an exact solution to the KG equation by employing a linear and vector potential energy [26].
In 2018, Boumali et al. investigated a two dimensional KG oscillator under the GUP [27].
In another study, Elviyanti et al. employed Asymptotic Iteration Method to examine the Hultén potential energy in the KG equation in the ML [28].

Additionally, in 2013, Menculini et al. studied the relativistic Landau problem in Dirac equation within the presence of the ML and reported an exact solution of the wave function in the momentum space [29].
In 2015, Pedram et al. studied the two dimensional Dirac equation by employing a non-varying magnetic field in an ML.
Ikot et al. examined the two-dimensional harmonic oscillator problem within the framework of ML on the Dirac equation in the commutative and noncommutative space, respectively [31].

In a very recent paper, Hamil et al. investigated the Dirac oscillator in two and three dimensions. They announced that their results could predict the upper bound of the GUP parameter of the relativistic Landau levels in graphene [32].
Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau (DKP) equation is another relativistic equation that appeared a century ago [33–36].

Moreover, before the 1970’s its solutions were considered to be equivalent to the KG and Proca equations in on-shell cases. However, after then, it was comprehended that in special cases that involve a symmetry breaking and hadronic processes, the solution of the DKP equation differs from those of other equations [37].
For example, Boumali et al. investigated a two dimensional DKP oscillator under the effect of a magnetic field [37].
Falek et al. investigated a three dimensional DKP oscillator [38].
